titleZh: 顧客逐漸流失

brief.meaningEn: Customers gradually stop using or returning to a business or service.
brief.meaningZh: 顧客逐步不再使用或光顧某生意或服務。
brief.grammar: customers drift away; customers may/will drift away; customers are drifting away; specify whether the departure is observed or predicted.
brief.register: Gradual-movement metaphor. It does not necessarily mean one formal complaint, a sudden mass exit or that every customer leaves.
brief.boundaryZh: 需保留逐漸、範圍及may/will等語氣；一次少人不能單獨證實長期流失，更不能直接定原因。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可觀察重複光顧減少，再問原因，不把沒有回來一概當不滿或永久離開。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述或預測逐漸流失，分清資料與推測。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Without reliable service, customers will drift away.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 30, table 1, row 2; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The case study suggests customers may drift away if appointment changes are not communicated, but it gives a warning about future loyalty rather than figures showing an actual decline.
listening.zh: 案例指預約改動若沒通知，顧客可能逐漸流失；它是在警告未來忠誠度，不是給已下降數據。
listening.promptZh: 敘述是甚麼性質？

options.en: A conditional warning about gradual loss, not measured decline already established.
options.zh: 關於逐步流失的有條件警告，不是已確立量度下降。

options.en: A completed count showing every regular customer has stopped returning.
options.zh: 已完成統計顯示每位熟客都停止回來。

options.en: A report that all appointment changes had been communicated successfully.
options.zh: 報告每項預約改動都已成功通知。

options.en: A decision by the service to reject returning customers.
options.zh: 服務拒絕回頭客的決定。

listening.explanationZh: may及if保留條件預測，未給已流失統計或主動拒客。

reply.promptZh: 案例擔心預約改動沒通知會怎樣？
reply.promptEn: What does the case study fear if appointment changes are not communicated?

options.en: People may gradually stop returning because they cannot rely on the arrangements.
options.zh: 大家可能因不能依賴安排而逐步不再回來。

options.en: Customers may drift away if changes are not communicated.
options.zh: 改動若沒通知，顧客可能逐漸流失。

options.en: The service risks losing repeat visits over time.
options.zh: 服務有隨時間失去重複光顧的風險。

options.en: It fears customers will return less often and their loyalty will weaken over time.
options.zh: 它擔心顧客回來次數逐少，忠誠度隨時間轉弱。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都答條件風險，沒有擅自報已有下降。

scene.promptZh: 小說描述小店幾個月內熟客回來次數逐漸少，店主還沒問原因；你想描述已給趨勢，不推所有人都永不回來。哪句準確？

options.en: Some regular customers are drifting away, though the reason still needs checking.
options.zh: 有些熟客正逐漸流失，原因仍需查。

options.en: The owner has already established that every customer left because of the prices.
options.zh: 店主已確立每位顧客都因價錢離開。

options.en: The account describes only a single cancelled visit, with no pattern over time.
options.zh: 敘述只描述一次取消，沒長期模式。

scene.explanationZh: 幾月逐少支持部分熟客流失，未確認原因，不是只有一次。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持已發生的 customers drift away？

options.en: A pattern of fewer repeat visits develops over several months.
options.zh: 數月逐步形成重複到訪減少模式。

options.en: A conditional warning mentions possible loss without observing any change yet.
options.zh: 有條件警告提可能流失，尚未觀察改變。

options.en: Customers gradually stop returning to the service.
options.zh: 顧客逐漸不再回來。

contrast.explanationZh: 可能警告不能當已發生的趨勢證據。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴把案例的may改成已流失一半顧客，但文中沒數據。哪句最好？

options.en: Keep the conditional warning and ask for evidence before adding a measured decline.
options.zh: 保留有條件警告，加量度下降前先找證據。

options.en: The warning is enough to estimate that half the customers have left.
options.zh: 警告已足以估一半顧客離開。

options.en: Since no decline is measured, the service should treat communication as irrelevant to future loyalty.
options.zh: 既沒量下降，服務就應把溝通當與未來忠誠度無關。

dialogue.explanationZh: 未量結果不容編比例，也不使條件風險變完全無關。

speaking.en: Customers may drift away over time, but we need evidence before reporting that the decline has happened.
speaking.zh: 顧客可能隨時間逐漸流失，但報下降已發生前需證據。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再區分預測及觀察。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：陶藝店發現以前固定預約修補示範的熟客，近幾季愈來愈少再報名。店準備新一輪自願參加的短示範，你想向同事提議發一封不施壓的邀請，讓舊客知道仍歡迎他們、毋須購物，不聲稱回信就是訂單。用一至兩句英文提議內部訊息。

examples.en: Some customers are drifting away from the repair demonstrations, so I suggest a welcoming invitation to the next short session. Make clear that they can simply watch without buying anything or promising to return regularly.
examples.zh: 一些顧客正逐漸不再參與修補示範，所以我建議友善邀他們參加下一場短活動；說清可只看、不購物或承諾定期再來。

examples.en: As customers drift away over successive seasons, we could remind former participants that the new demonstration is open to them without any purchase. Let us offer a choice, rather than treat a reply as a confirmed order.
examples.zh: 顧客幾季逐漸流失，我們可提醒以前參加者，新示範歡迎他們且不用購物；提供選擇，不把回信當確定訂單。

writing.selfCheckZh: 根據多季參與下降提出友善自選的舊客邀請，列免購物及無定期承諾，不把回覆變成交或強求回來。

takeaways.en: Customers drift away when repeated disappointments make them choose another service.
takeaways.zh: 反覆失望讓顧客選另一服務時，顧客逐漸流失。

takeaways.en: The story shows customers drifting away before the owner begins asking why they no longer return.
takeaways.zh: 故事展示顧客逐漸流失，之後店主才開始問為何不再回來。

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese translations checked against each English sentence; not independent human approval.

titleZh: 基本環節失靈，難以維持

brief.meaningEn: Essential practical parts or habits of cooperation stop working together or become unreliable.
brief.meaningZh: 必要的實際環節或合作習慣不再協調運作，或變得不可靠。
brief.grammar: if the basics fall apart; the basics fell/have fallen apart; specify which essentials are failing.
brief.register: Productive use of the conventional fall-apart metaphor. Basics is context-dependent; the wording does not itself identify the cause or make every part fail.
brief.boundaryZh: 需指出基本環節及失效跡象，不只是裝飾不好；也不由幾項失靈推每人能力或所有材料都無價值。
brief.misconceptionZh: 成果外觀可好，接收交付等基本流程仍可能失效；要看實際運作。
brief.outcomeZh: 能具體描述基本工作怎失靈及仍可保留的部分。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The project will fail if the basics fall apart.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 30, table 1, row 5; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: At the exhibition desk, the basics were falling apart: arrival notes were not reaching the hosts, labels did not match the boxes and nobody knew which list was current, although the artwork itself was ready.
listening.zh: 展覽櫃檯基本環節正失靈：到達便條沒送到接待者、標籤對不上箱、沒人知哪版清單最新，雖作品本身備好。
listening.promptZh: 基本環節的問題在哪裏？

options.en: Information, labels and current-list control were failing, while the artwork was ready.
options.zh: 資訊、標籤及最新清單管理失靈，作品已備好。

options.en: The artwork was unfinished but all desk information was current.
options.zh: 作品未完，櫃檯資訊則全是最新。

options.en: Only the visual decoration at the desk was being criticised.
options.zh: 只批評櫃檯外觀裝飾。

options.en: The team had already replaced all the mismatched labels and confirmed the current list.
options.zh: 團隊已換全部錯標、確認最新清單。

listening.explanationZh: 三項操作失靈具體交代basics，不是藝術品或外觀問題，也未說已修。

reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你說櫃檯基本環節失靈？
reply.promptEn: Why do you say the essential desk arrangements were failing?

options.en: Notes were not reaching hosts, labels mismatched boxes and the current list was unclear.
options.zh: 便條未到接待者、標籤錯箱、最新清單不明。

options.en: The basics were falling apart across the information and handover process.
options.zh: 資訊及交接程序的基本環節正失靈。

options.en: The desk could not reliably connect the right information with the right items.
options.zh: 櫃檯不能可靠地把正確資料連到正確物件。

options.en: Several essential coordination steps were no longer working as needed.
options.zh: 幾個必要協調步驟不再按需要運作。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都給基本流程失效，不否定已備作品。

scene.promptZh: 班級旅行宣傳片已做好，集合地點卻有兩個版本、聯絡人未定、點名表不齊，出發仍未到。哪句貼切？

options.en: The basics are falling apart even though the promotional film is ready.
options.zh: 宣傳片雖備好，基本環節仍正失靈。

options.en: The promotional film confirms that the meeting and attendance arrangements are complete.
options.zh: 宣傳片確認集合及點名安排已完成。

options.en: The only remaining task is to change the music in the completed film.
options.zh: 唯一剩餘工作是改完成影片的音樂。

scene.explanationZh: 集合聯絡點名是必要實務，影片完成不能替代它們。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 the basics fall apart？

options.en: Essential information no longer reaches the people who need it.
options.zh: 必要資料不再到需用者手上。

options.en: A team changes the decorative border while core arrangements remain reliable.
options.zh: 核心安排仍可靠，只改裝飾邊框。

options.en: Key items cannot be matched with their instructions or current records.
options.zh: 關鍵物件對不上指引或現紀錄。

contrast.explanationZh: 只改外觀而核心可靠，不是基本環節失靈。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說作品備好就代表櫃檯也準備妥，但便條及箱標仍錯。哪句最好？

options.en: The artwork and the desk process have different statuses; we still need to repair the information handover.
options.zh: 作品及櫃檯程序狀態不同，仍需修資訊交接。

options.en: We should count the desk ready because the most visible part is finished.
options.zh: 最顯眼部分完成，所以應把櫃檯算備妥。

options.en: Rehearse the presentation again before deciding who receives the arrival notes at the desk.
options.zh: 決定誰在櫃檯收抵達便條前，再排練一次展示。

dialogue.explanationZh: 作品已備好，資訊交接仍失靈，需處理收便條及核箱標等基本流程；不以顯眼成果代準備，也不再先排已備妥部分。

speaking.en: The basics are falling apart, so we need to identify the essential steps that are no longer reliable.
speaking.zh: 基本環節正失靈，所以需找出哪些必要步驟不再可靠。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再具體指出失效環節。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你與同伴修改家庭短劇，華麗聚餐背後，家人已不再聽彼此說話、答應的事常不做；你想向編劇說是關係的基本互動失靈，不只餐桌不整齊。你提議結尾加一次真正聽完對方的嘗試，不假裝一幕就修好所有關係。用一至兩句英文寫意見。

examples.en: The basics are falling apart in this family: they no longer listen or keep their promises, however beautiful the party looks. I would end with one genuine attempt to hear the other person, not an instant reconciliation.
examples.zh: 這家庭基本互動正失靈：聚餐再美，他們已不聽或守承諾；我會以一次真心聽對方的嘗試作結，不是立即和好。

examples.en: We should show that the basics have fallen apart between the characters, rather than blame the untidy table. A small moment of listening could begin a change without pretending everything is repaired.
examples.zh: 應展示角色間基本互動已失靈，不是怪餐桌不整齊；一刻聆聽可開始改變，不假裝一切修好。

writing.selfCheckZh: 從互聽與守承諾指出關係基本互動失靈，提出結尾的小改變，不把問題歸裝飾或以一幕保證全修復。

takeaways.en: The basics fell apart when the team lost track of the current plan and who was responsible.
takeaways.zh: 團隊不知最新計劃及誰負責時，基本環節失靈。

takeaways.en: A polished presentation will not help much if the basics fall apart behind it.
takeaways.zh: 背後基本環節失靈時，精緻呈現也幫不了太多。

english.evidence: Read every model, option and example for sense, grammar, contextual fit and target morphology; not independent human approval.

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese translations checked against each English sentence; not independent human approval.

titleZh: 不再留意需要關注的事

brief.meaningEn: Stop paying attention to something that needs continued attention.
brief.meaningZh: 不再留意原本需持續關注的事情。
brief.grammar: take your eye off + matter needing attention; took/taken; the abstract object makes the visual-attention metaphor clear.
brief.register: Productive visual-attention wording, related to the fixed take your eye off the ball idiom. Here the named object identifies the actual responsibility.
brief.boundaryZh: 本課抽象事務的注意力，不只是眼睛移開；暫停某一時段不必等於失責，需看事情仍需誰關注及有否交接。
brief.misconceptionZh: 其他部分順利，不表示可忘掉尚未解的關鍵部分；可安排具體檢視或交接。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指明被忽略的責任，分清注意力及實際狀態。
brief.sourceClassificationNote: The guide labels the fragment a set phrase. The lesson treats eye-off-plus-abstract-object as a productive visual metaphor. Oxford eye_1 and Cambridge take-eye-off-the-ball attest the related fixed ball idiom; this does not falsely claim every replacement object is a new fixed idiom.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Do not take your eye off the budget during expansion.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 30, table 1, row 7; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: I took my eye off the return dates while organising the display, and only noticed later that two borrowed items were overdue; the successful opening had distracted me from that responsibility.
listening.zh: 我忙辦展示時沒留意歸還日期，後來才發現兩件借物過期；成功開幕令我忽略那責任。
listening.promptZh: 被忽略的是甚麼，後來發現甚麼？

options.en: Return dates were overlooked, and two borrowed items became overdue.
options.zh: 歸還日被忽略，兩件借物過期。

options.en: The display failed to open because its materials had not arrived.
options.zh: 展示因材料未到而未開。

options.en: All borrowed items were returned before the opening.
options.zh: 開幕前所有借物都已還。

options.en: The speaker had handed the dates to a colleague who completed every return.
options.zh: 說話者已把日期交同事，對方完成每項歸還。

listening.explanationZh: 歸還日期是仍需注意的責任，展示成功不代表歸還已完或已交接。

reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼較後才知道有借物過期？
reply.promptEn: Why did you only notice the overdue items later?

options.en: The display work distracted me from checking the return dates.
options.zh: 展示工作令我分心，沒核歸還日。

options.en: I took my eye off the return dates while concentrating on the opening.
options.zh: 我專注開幕時不再留意歸還日。

options.en: I kept focusing on the visible event instead of the outstanding borrowing responsibilities.
options.zh: 我一直專注可見活動，不是未完借物責任。

options.en: The dates still needed attention, but I had not reviewed them during the preparations.
options.zh: 日期仍需留意，但準備期間我沒檢視。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代忽略的部分及注意力轉移。

scene.promptZh: 你們看重演出流暢，卻沒再留意尚未確認的字幕來源，現在想提醒同伴不要因彩排順就忽略。哪句貼切？

options.en: We should not take our eye off the caption sources just because the rehearsal went well.
options.zh: 不能只因彩排順利，就不再留意字幕來源。

options.en: Use the remaining rehearsal time only to improve fluency, and leave source checking until the public performance.
options.zh: 餘下彩排時間只改善流暢度，來源核對留公開演出時。

options.en: The sources are no longer part of the production responsibilities.
options.zh: 來源不再屬製作責任。

scene.explanationZh: 彩排順利不能代來源核對；仍需安排注意力，不能只顧流暢或把來源移出責任。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持本課 take your eye off？

options.en: An unresolved responsibility receives no further attention while another task dominates.
options.zh: 另一任務佔注意力，未解責任沒再被留意。

options.en: A responsibility is clearly handed over and the designated person continues checking it.
options.zh: 責任清楚交接，指定人持續核對。

options.en: A person overlooks needed follow-up while focusing on the more visible result.
options.zh: 某人專注較顯眼成果，忽略所需跟進。

contrast.explanationZh: 有人持續負責的交接，不等於事情被忽略。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說開幕成功就可把借物一事擱下，但仍有兩件未還。哪句最好？

options.en: The opening went well, but the outstanding returns still need an owner and a date.
options.zh: 開幕順利，但未完歸還仍需負責人及日期。

options.en: Prepare another display first and review the overdue returns only after its opening.
options.zh: 先備另一展示，開幕後才檢視逾期歸還。

options.en: We should check the display feedback again before deciding whether the return dates matter.
options.zh: 應先再看展示回饋，才定歸還日是否重要。

dialogue.explanationZh: 已有兩件逾期需具體負責人及日期，不應再被新展示或舊回饋分走注意。

speaking.en: We should not take our eye off the remaining responsibility just because the most visible part went well.
speaking.zh: 不能只因最顯眼部分順利，就不再留意剩餘責任。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再指明仍需關注的部分。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你幫朋友準備婚禮，現已完成音樂清單，但有長輩的接送安排仍未確認。你想把剩餘責任有禮交接給一位同伴，請他明晚前核司機，不是說音樂不值得做。用一至兩句英文發訊息。
writing.selfCheckZh: 肯定音樂完成，清楚交代仍需接送核對、請同伴接責任及期限，不把成果當其餘責任已消失。

examples.en: We must not take our eye off the transport for the older relatives now that the music list is ready. Could you check the driver by tomorrow evening and let us know?
examples.zh: 音樂清單好後，不能不再留意長輩交通；你可明晚前核司機並告訴我們嗎？

examples.en: I am glad the music is sorted, but I do not want us to take our eye off the unconfirmed pickup. Could you take responsibility for checking it before tomorrow evening?
examples.zh: 音樂安排好我很高興，但不想我們忽略未確認接送；你可負責明晚前核它嗎？

takeaways.en: They took their eye off the unresolved permissions while polishing the final design.
takeaways.zh: 他們修飾最後設計時，忽略了未解許可。

takeaways.en: I can hand the task over clearly rather than take my eye off it and assume someone else will notice.
takeaways.zh: 我可清楚交接任務，不是忽略它並假定別人會發現。

titleZh: 競爭對手不會一直停在原地

brief.meaningEn: Rivals continue changing or developing rather than remaining in a fixed state.
brief.meaningZh: 對手會繼續改變或發展，不是維持不變狀態。
brief.grammar: competition never stands still, so...; competition refers collectively to rivals, and never makes the warning emphatic.
brief.register: Rhetorical personification used to encourage attention to change. It is not a measured claim that every rival improves at every moment.
brief.boundaryZh: 強調不宜假定對手永遠不變，不表示人人每刻都進步、自己必輸或需盲目跟每個改動；仍需核實。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可以了解新做法再按自身目標判斷，不由競爭變動直接推勝負。
brief.outcomeZh: 能理解勸人留意變化的修辭，分清一般警醒與實際比較結果。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A company must adapt because competition never stands still.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 30, table 1, row 10; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: The workshop owner said competition never stands still after nearby services began offering later appointments; she wanted to review what her customers needed before deciding whether to change her own hours.
listening.zh: 附近服務開始提供較晚預約後，工作室店主說競爭不會一直停在原地；她想先看客人需要，再定是否改自己時間。
listening.promptZh: 這警醒引出甚麼決定程序？

options.en: Notice rivals’ changed hours, then review customer needs before deciding.
options.zh: 留意對手改時間，再看客人需要後決定。

options.en: Copy the later hours immediately without checking the workshop’s customers.
options.zh: 不查本店客人，立即照搬較晚時間。

options.en: Report that the new appointments have already made every rival more successful.
options.zh: 報新預約已讓每個對手更成功。

options.en: Assume nearby services will keep their original hours indefinitely.
options.zh: 假定附近服務永遠維持原時間。

listening.explanationZh: 對手改是觀察，先看客需再決定是回應，未給勝負或必須照搬。

reply.promptZh: 店主為甚麼想重新看客人的時間需要？
reply.promptEn: Why did the owner want to review customers’ timing needs?

options.en: Nearby services had begun offering later appointments.
options.zh: 附近服務開始提供較晚預約。

options.en: Competition never stands still, and the new appointment options prompted her review.
options.zh: 競爭不會一直停在原地，新預約選項促使她檢視。

options.en: The options available to customers were changing.
options.zh: 客人可選的選項正在改。

options.en: She did not want to assume the surrounding services had stayed the same.
options.zh: 她不想假定周邊服務仍一樣。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都給外界選項改變，不保證需改或已輸。

scene.promptZh: 故事中兩隊做同類解謎活動，其中一隊新增可預先試玩的版本，另一隊想先體驗再看是否合自己觀眾，不直接照抄。哪句準確？

options.en: Competition never stands still, so we should understand the new option before deciding what suits our audience.
options.zh: 競爭不會一直停在原地，所以應先了解新選項，再定甚麼合我們觀眾。

options.en: The preview must suit our audience because it is already popular with the rival team’s visitors.
options.zh: 預試版既受對方訪客歡迎，就必適合我們觀眾。

options.en: We can judge the changed format by the rival’s reputation without trying the preview ourselves.
options.zh: 不用親自試預試版，靠對方聲譽就可判新形式。

scene.explanationZh: 競爭新做法需了解，再按自己的觀眾評估；對方受歡迎或有名，不代實際體驗及合用判斷。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜把 competition never stands still 理解成？

options.en: A warning against assuming rivals remain unchanged.
options.zh: 警醒不應假定對手不變。

options.en: A measured guarantee that every rival improves continuously at the same rate.
options.zh: 量度保證每位對手持續以同速進步。

options.en: A reason to check what has actually changed.
options.zh: 查實際改了甚麼的理由。

contrast.explanationZh: 修辭警醒不提供所有對手的持續進步數據。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說「對手改晚間預約，我們今晚就全改」，但還未知自己的客需及人手。哪句最好？

options.en: Check our customers and capacity before choosing a response to the new hours.
options.zh: 回應新時間前，先查我們客需及能力。

options.en: The rival’s change is enough to confirm our customers want the same hours.
options.zh: 對手改動已足以確認我們客人想同樣時間。

options.en: We should avoid learning anything about the new service so we do not get distracted.
options.zh: 應避免了解新服務任何內容，以免分心。

dialogue.explanationZh: 留意不等於照搬，也不是完全迴避新資料；自身需要及能力仍重要。

speaking.en: Competition never stands still, but we should check the evidence before deciding which change matters to us.
speaking.zh: 競爭不會一直停在原地，但應先查證據，再定哪改動與我們有關。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再保留觀察與回應的判斷。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你替校際戲劇隊寫賀卡，肯定他們去年奪獎，也想邀大家下月繼續排新作，因其他隊伍仍在發展。你不想把提醒寫成去年勝利無價值或今年必輸，也不要求照抄別隊。用一至兩句英文賀詞及邀請。

examples.en: Congratulations on last year’s award; competition never stands still, so I hope we will keep developing our next production together. Shall we begin rehearsing the new piece next month?
examples.zh: 恭喜去年得獎；競爭不會停在原地，所以希望我們繼續一起發展下個作品。下月開始排新作好嗎？

examples.en: We can celebrate the award and remember that competition never stands still. I would love us to meet next month and begin a new piece, without treating last year’s result as a promise about this year.
examples.zh: 我們可慶祝得獎，也記得競爭不會停在原地；我很想下月聚起開始新作，不把去年結果當今年承諾。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把賀獎及邀新作排練連起，肯定過去又保留對手仍發展，不預判今年勝負或要求照搬。

takeaways.en: The owner reminds the team that competition never stands still before asking what has changed since the last review.
takeaways.zh: 問上次檢視後改了甚麼前，店主提醒團隊競爭不會一直停在原地。

takeaways.en: Competition never stands still, so old comparisons may need checking rather than repeating unchanged.
takeaways.zh: 競爭不會一直停在原地，所以舊比較可能需重核，不是原樣重述。

titleZh: 遇到問題或困難

brief.meaningEn: Encounter difficulties or problems during an activity.
brief.meaningZh: 在進行事情時遇到困難或問題。
brief.grammar: run into trouble with + task/when + clause; ran/has run into trouble; identify the problem rather than only saying trouble.
brief.register: Established encounter phrase, figurative here. It does not necessarily mean deliberate wrongdoing, punishment or an irreversible failure.
brief.boundaryZh: 遇問題不等於一定犯法、受罰或最後失敗；需按情境指出是甚麼問題及後續。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可遇到困難仍找出替代，不把麻煩當已全完或全部取消。
brief.outcomeZh: 能自然描述遇到的具體問題並說下一步。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Small firms can run into trouble when stock is poorly managed.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 30, table 1, row 11; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: We ran into trouble when the recording files would not open on the classroom computer, but a colleague brought a compatible player before the lesson began.
listening.zh: 錄音檔在課室電腦開不了，我們遇到問題；但同事在上課前帶了兼容播放器。
listening.promptZh: 遇到甚麼問題，後來怎樣？

options.en: The files would not open, and another player provided a workable option before class.
options.zh: 檔開不了，另一播放器在上課前提供可行選項。

options.en: The team was punished for deliberately deleting the files.
options.zh: 團隊因故意刪檔受罰。

options.en: The lesson was cancelled before anyone considered another player.
options.zh: 未考慮另一播放器前，課已取消。

options.en: The classroom computer opened the files normally throughout.
options.zh: 課室電腦一直正常開檔。

listening.explanationZh: 開檔困難是trouble，同事替代解一步，不是處罰或已取消。

reply.promptZh: 課前出了甚麼問題？
reply.promptEn: What problem came up before the lesson?

options.en: The classroom computer could not open the recordings.
options.zh: 課室電腦開不了錄音。

options.en: We ran into trouble with the files and needed another player.
options.zh: 檔案令我們遇問題，需另一播放器。

options.en: The available software did not work with the recordings.
options.zh: 現有軟件不合錄音檔。

options.en: We had a compatibility problem before the colleague brought an alternative.
options.zh: 同事帶替代前，我們有兼容問題。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都答具體遇困，不擅自加責怪或違規。

scene.promptZh: 你們做訪問集，發現兩位受訪者給不同日期，現需回查而非直接放棄。哪句貼切？

options.en: We have run into trouble with the dates and need to compare the records.
options.zh: 我們在日期遇問題，需比較紀錄。

options.en: The different dates confirm both interviewees deliberately lied.
options.zh: 日期不同確認兩受訪者故意說謊。

options.en: The disagreement has already been resolved in the final checked version.
options.zh: 分歧已在最後核妥版解決。

scene.explanationZh: 日期分歧是待查問題，不確立動機或已解。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 ran into trouble 單獨得出？

options.en: Some difficulty was encountered.
options.zh: 遇到某些困難。

options.en: The people deliberately broke a rule and were punished.
options.zh: 當事人故意違規，並受處罰。

options.en: Context can identify the problem and whether it was resolved.
options.zh: 情境可指出問題及有否解決。

contrast.explanationZh: 這用法只說遇難，不自帶違規處罰。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把檔案開不了寫成團隊被罰，但沒有違規情節。哪句最好？

options.en: Describe the compatibility problem and the alternative player, without adding misconduct.
options.zh: 描述兼容問題及替代播放器，不加違規。

options.en: The word trouble is enough to include a punishment in the account.
options.zh: trouble一字已足以在敘述加處罰。

options.en: Since another player worked, we should say there was no earlier difficulty.
options.zh: 既另一播放器可用，就應說早先沒困難。

dialogue.explanationZh: 遇困與做錯事不同，替代成功也不抹去原先問題。

speaking.en: We ran into trouble, but the next step was to identify the difficulty rather than assume the whole task had failed.
speaking.zh: 我們遇問題，但下一步是辨困難，不是假定整項任務失敗。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再具體指出遇到的問題。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你本想替朋友改一件舊外套，拆開才發現裏布比原先看到的破得更大，你沒有剪掉它，也未承諾當天能修。你想有禮通知朋友遇到問題，請他先看照片再商量範圍，不直接說外套沒用。用一至兩句英文發訊息。
writing.selfCheckZh: 具體交代新見裏布問題及尚未剪動，請確認修補範圍，不把遇困變整件無用或當天必修好。

examples.en: I have run into trouble with the lining: the tear is larger than it first appeared. Could you look at the photographs so we can agree what to repair before I go further?
examples.zh: 我在裏布遇問題：破口比最初看到大；可否看照片，讓我們議修甚麼後我再繼續？

examples.en: I ran into trouble after opening the coat and finding more damage inside. I have not cut anything away, and I would like to discuss the repair with you first.
examples.zh: 拆開外套發現內裏更大破損，我遇到問題；我沒剪走任何部分，想先跟你談修補。

takeaways.en: They ran into trouble when the instructions did not match the parts in the box.
takeaways.zh: 指引對不上箱內零件時，他們遇到問題。

takeaways.en: If we run into trouble with the draft, we can ask which part the reader found confusing.
takeaways.zh: 草稿遇問題時，可問讀者覺哪部分難明。

titleZh: 很快就完成或發生

brief.meaningEn: Very quickly or after a very short time.
brief.meaningZh: 很快，或經很短時間後。
brief.grammar: finish/find/arrive in no time; often informal exaggeration; context identifies which action was quick.
brief.register: Established informal time phrase. It is not an exact duration or a promise that every later task will be equally fast.
brief.boundaryZh: 需分清快的是哪步，不把一項很快推全項目已完；也不保證其他人或下次同速。
brief.misconceptionZh: 短時間完成某步仍可留下檢查或其他工作，不能用快就代準確。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用自然口語描述快速完成，保留範圍及後續。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: With practice, she finished the task in no time.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page 30, table 1, row 12; source book/question/sample not stated where null.

listening.en: With the boxes numbered clearly, we found the missing folder in no time, but we still needed to check whether its notes matched the current plan.
listening.zh: 箱號清楚，我們很快找到失夾，但仍需核筆記是否合最新計劃。
listening.promptZh: 哪步很快，哪步仍待做？

options.en: Finding the folder was quick; checking the notes against the current plan remained.
options.zh: 找夾很快；對照最新計劃核筆記仍待做。

options.en: Every note had already been checked and approved.
options.zh: 每項筆記已核並批妥。

options.en: The team spent the whole day searching because the box numbers were missing.
options.zh: 箱號不見，所以團隊花全天找。

options.en: The current plan was rewritten before the folder was located.
options.zh: 找到夾前，最新計劃已重寫。

listening.explanationZh: 箱號幫快速找到，不等於筆記已核或計劃已改。

reply.promptZh: 箱號清楚有甚麼幫助？
reply.promptEn: How did clear box numbers help?

options.en: We found the missing folder very quickly.
options.zh: 我們很快找到失夾。

options.en: We located it in no time instead of searching through every box.
options.zh: 我們很快找到它，不用找遍每箱。

options.en: The numbers made it easy to identify where the folder belonged.
options.zh: 號碼讓我們容易辨夾在哪。

options.en: The search took only a short time once we used the box numbers.
options.zh: 用了箱號後，搜尋只花很短時間。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說搜尋速度，不把快找到當核內容已完。

scene.promptZh: 同伴用清楚目錄一下便找到想讀的章，但還沒讀完書。哪句準確？

options.en: She found the chapter in no time, though she has not finished the book.
options.zh: 她很快找到那章，雖尚未看完書。

options.en: The catalogue search took most of the session, leaving no time to start reading the chapter.
options.zh: 目錄搜尋花了大部分活動時間，沒時間開始看那章。

options.en: She could not locate the chapter and gave up the search.
options.zh: 她找不到章，放棄搜尋。

scene.explanationZh: in no time說找到章很快，未說閱讀已完成；也不符合搜尋佔大部分時間或找不到。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 finished one task in no time 得出？

options.en: That task was completed very quickly.
options.zh: 該任務很快完成。

options.en: All other tasks have also been completed at the same speed.
options.zh: 其他任務也已以同速完成。

options.en: The wording is informal rather than an exact stopwatch measurement.
options.zh: 措辭屬口語，不是精確計時量度。

contrast.explanationZh: 一項很快不確立其他部分結果。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說失夾很快找到，所以內容就不用核；你知計劃改過。哪句最好？

options.en: Finding it was quick, but we still need to check its notes against the changed plan.
options.zh: 找到很快，但仍需對改過計劃核筆記。

options.en: Use the notes for the newer plan without comparing them, since the folder was indexed under the project name.
options.zh: 文件夾按項目名編索引，所以不用比較就把筆記用於新計劃。

options.en: We should use the old notes first and compare them only after the event.
options.zh: 應先用舊筆記，活動後才比較。

dialogue.explanationZh: 索引幫快速找到，不反映筆記已更新至新計劃；使用前仍需比對，不留活動後才查。

speaking.en: We found it in no time, but locating the file was only the first part of the work.
speaking.zh: 我們很快找到它，但找檔只是工作第一部分。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再交代快速的是哪一步。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友為生日卡急找裝飾，你熟悉摺一種紙花，可以很快做三朵，卻沒時間包辦整場布置。你想主動提出這一小項幫助，請他選顏色，不把快做紙花說成所有準備都已完。用一至兩句英文提出幫忙。

examples.en: I can make three paper flowers in no time because I know the fold well. What colours would you like for the card?
examples.zh: 我熟悉摺法，可很快做三朵紙花；卡片你想用甚麼顏色？

examples.en: The paper flowers should be ready in no time, so I can help with that part of the card. I cannot take on the whole room decoration, but you can choose the colours for these three.
examples.zh: 紙花應很快做好，所以我可幫卡片那部分；我不能接整場布置，但這三朵顏色可由你選。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以熟悉摺法說可快做三朵的有限幫忙，問顏色並保留不包整場，不把預計速度變已全部完成。

takeaways.en: The clear index helped us find the right section in no time.
takeaways.zh: 清楚索引幫我們很快找到正確部分。

takeaways.en: She prepared a simple example in no time, then checked whether it answered the learner’s question.
takeaways.zh: 她很快備簡單例子，再核是否答學習者問題。
